column2: The comparers' rehearsal run. The copy runs without the news item (0x767330), without the award record (0x86c8c0) and without the club lists (0x842c00), because these allocate and cannot run twice.

The rehearsal of the news item. The random draws come from the original routine's tape (n and the answer) and, instead of delivering the news, the copy records the destination (1 the player's club, 2 the club's nation, 0 none). The tape keeps the next position and whether any n did not match.

Byte +0xc (repeated case) of the absence record. \n 0x41a360 does not write it: the 13-byte record is built in a local and +0xc keeps whatever the previous call left in the dword E−0x10 of the stack (E: esp on entry). On the original routine's normal path, through game_check_players_missing_training (0x5d6aa0), the previous call that reaches that depth is 0x54cdb0 (days since arrival), which stores its `this` there, the game date 0xae2c90: the low byte is 0x90. \n The copy uses that value (a repeated case); the comparer does not compare it (the original's value is genuine residue).

Moves a fixture's date to tomorrow if it is not after today, then adds the fixture to the fixture calendar. \n The fixture date (+0x2a day, +0x28 year, from the dwords the original routine pushes: 0x549ef0 push year; push day; lea ecx, local -> thiscall, ret 8) that is not after today ([0xae2c90]: unsigned year, signed day) becomes tomorrow (0x54c5b0: push 1; push output; mov ecx, 0xae2c90 -> thiscall(date, output, n), ret 8); and the fixture goes to the calendar (0x5aa680: push 1; push &fixture; ecx = [0xae2a58] -> thiscall, ret 8).

True when the competition gets no draw news item. \n That is the case with fewer than 2 ties, with rule 0x200 (+0xd), for the special national-team competition (0x76d940 on [0xb74318]: push comp; ecx = the national teams; no add esp -> ret 4; the Rust copy is stdcall(comp)) or for a friendly (0x5c6710 on [0xae2c74]: push comp; ecx = the Friendly -> thiscall, ret 4).

Core of 0x5219b0: collects the clubs that can play one side of a fixture, descending to feeder ties for empty sides; returns the count. 
 The fixture is match `jogo` of round `rodada` ([[+0xad] + rodada × 4] + jogo × 0x35). Each side (+0 and +2) that has a club goes to `saida[*conta]` (and the count goes up); an empty side (−1) descends to the match it comes from (+0xe/+0xa and +0x10/+0xc). 
 A negative round or match −1 (also during the descents): the error box (line 0x1592, if `caixa`) and the count. 
 Returns the count.

Writes one group round (a 0x41-byte record, like the league rounds). \n The date goes through 0x68a160 (day, month with 0 = January, weekday, code), with no years to add and value 0; and match 0 is left empty (0x68a1c0 with −1, −1, −1 and value 0).

Side-by-side comparer of create_schedule. \n The original routine runs with the caller's outputs, the copy with its own outputs that start with the same values, both from the same [0xb67a34]; the outputs and the bytes written to the two tables must be equal; the copy's table is freed (0x9452ca). \n In the stage without a table only the original runs (neither writes anything; the outputs may not even exist).

`BraCup::build_team_table()` (0x427c20, thiscall, ret 0, bra_cup.cpp): sets +0x3e = 71 and builds the team table from the entrant list; returns 1. \n The team table is allocated with 0x944e46 (0x1aa bytes) at +0xa7; when out of memory, the error box for line 0x143 and −1. Each slot i (6 bytes) receives the club of entry i of the list at +0x14 (6 bytes), status +5 = 0xff and class +4 = 0. \n Returns 1.

Writes one cup round (a 0x68-byte record, docs/.md §2.4). \n The draw (day, month with 0 = January, years to add to the cup year +0x40, weekday or −1) goes through 0x521e60; the match (the same, plus the leg at +6 and the venue at +0x13) through 0x521eb0. \n Then the fields: +7 the round name, +9 the index, +0xb the draw bits, +0xd and +0xf the tie-breakers (single match and two legs), +0x17 the category copied into each match, +0x18/+0x1a/+0x1c/+0x1e teams, matches, new teams and entrants already in, +0x20/+0x21/+0x22 replay, matches per tie and days between them, +0x5c/+0x60/+0x64 the prize money (reaching, winning, losing).

Builds the FA Cup round table, adjusting team, match and entrant counts by `b`, the entry mode and the entrants. 
 Here `b` = +0xb3 (signed byte), `entrada` = +0xb4 and `inscritos` = +0x3e (16-bit counts). 
 With +0xb4 = 1, the 1st round proper has 0x28 teams, 0x13 matches and no new teams, and the 2nd has 0x40 teams, 0x20 matches, 0x2b new teams and 0x6c entrants. Otherwise, the first has 6b + 0x28 teams, 3b + 0x14 matches, 6b new teams and 0x6c entrants, and the second (0x10 − b) × 4 teams, (0x10 − b) × 2 matches, 0x2c − 7b new teams and (b + 0x12) × 6 entrants. 
 The 3rd has (0x10 − b) × 2 teams and 0x10 − b matches; the 4th, b new teams and +0x3e − b entrants.

Frees the season tables before rebuilding them. \n It frees the entrant list (+0xa7), the rounds table (+0xa3) and the per-round ties (+0xad, one vector per round, +0x3c rounds), each one only if it exists (0x9452ca, cdecl). The pointers are left as they are (the following routines rebuild them).

Shared body of virtual +0x3c (`create_round_table(fase, &rodadas, &extra, &saida)`, thiscall, ret 0x10) of the single-stage cups: only stage −1 builds the round table. \n Outside stage −1 (the byte), returns 0 without writing anything. In −1: saida (if requested) = 0, rodadas = the table size, extra = 0; the table (0x944e46 of 0x68 × rodadas; when out of memory, the error box `linha` of `arquivo` and returns 0) is filled with each round. \n Returns the table.

`FraSuper::select_teams()` (0x5bf770, thiscall, ret 0, fra_super.cpp): picks the First Division champion and the French Cup winner, or the First Division runner-up when they are the same club. \n Sets +0x3e = 2 and allocates the list (0x944e46 of 0xc at +0xa7; when out of memory, the error box for line 0xc4 and −1). The First Division champion ([0x9cf5cc]; if missing, error box 0xcd and 0) and the French Cup winner ([0x9cf70c]; if missing, 0xd6 and 0); if they are the same club, the second one becomes the First Division runner-up (if missing, 0xe2 and 0). \n Class and status 0 for both; returns 1.

Runs only the original routine and checks the plan made beforehand. \n Simplification: 0x687430 allocates the form and the head-to-head of each row and the news item goes to the human players, so it cannot run twice. \n The check: returns 1, +0x3e = n, the table at +0xb1 holds the first n entrants in its rows (of 0x3b bytes), in order, and the first n slots of +0xee are zeroed.

Advances an Italian cup to the next stage (`advance_stage`, virtual +0x28). \n On the last stage (+0x30 ≥ +0x2c − 1, signed), the error box and nothing else. Otherwise +0x30 goes up by one and, on reaching `ultimo_grupo` + 1 (the end of the groups), it builds the knockout (`mata_mata`, direct call with the cup's ecx -> thiscall, ret 0).

Builds the knockout stage (Cup_Stage) with the `n` teams of `times`, frees the temporaries and draws the first round. \n The rounds come from the cup's method +0x3c (push 0; push &extra; push &rodadas; push fase; mov ecx -> thiscall, ret 0x10). The stage (0x944cf1(0xb2), cdecl; Cup_Stage::Cup_Stage 0x522e00, thiscall, ret 0x3c: the cup, n, the vector, the rounds (word), +4, the round table, the year +0x40 (word), the stage, 1, the extra (word), 0x14, 0, 0, 0 and `sementes`; the original routine pushes the words with garbage in the high 16 bits, which the constructor does not read) goes into [+0xc][fase]; the vector and the round table are freed (0x9452ca, cdecl; in this order). \n Without a stage, the error box for `linha`; with one, the draw of the first round (Cup::draw_round 0x51c410: push 0; mov ecx, stage -> thiscall, ret 4).

Side-by-side comparer of create_schedule. \n The original routine runs with the caller's outputs, the copy with its own outputs that start with the same values, both from the same [0xb67a34]; the outputs and the bytes written to the two tables (group or knockout tables, according to the copy's é_liga) must be equal; the copy's table is freed (0x9452ca).

`ItaCCup::select_entrants()` (0x63dfe0, thiscall, ret 0, ita_c_cup.cpp): the 90 entrants of the Serie C Cup from C1 and C2, reordered, shuffled and sorted by longitude into groups. 
 Sets +0xf2 = 0x5a and allocates the list of 0x168 bytes at +0xee (when out of memory, the error box for line 0x322 and 0). It takes the Italian clubs of C1 and C2 ([0x9cf578]..[0x9cf588]) in table order, up to 90. 
 Of the first 80, those relegated from Serie B ([0x9cf574]) and those from C1 that finished 4th, 5th or 6th go, one by one, to slots 80, 81... (swapped with whatever was there). 
 The first 80 are shuffled (0x4afb40), sorted by longitude (qsort with 0x53fe50) and each of their 8 groups of ten is shuffled (the regional groups [inference]); the last 10 slots stay as they are. Returns 1.

Shared body of virtual +0x3c (`create_round_table(fase, &rodadas, &extra, &saida)`, thiscall, ret 0x10) of the single-stage cups: only stage −1 builds the round table. \n Outside stage −1 (the byte), returns 0 without writing anything. In −1: saida (if requested) = 0, rodadas = the table size, extra = 0; the table (0x944e46 of 0x68 × rodadas; when out of memory, the error box `linha` of `arquivo` and returns 0) is filled with each round. \n Returns the table.

`JapEmpCup::collect_entrants()` (0x6624f0, thiscall, ret 0, jap_emp_cup.cpp): the 80 entrants of the Emperor's Cup, from the Japanese lower divisions (shuffled), then the J2 and J1 clubs. 
 Sets +0x3e = 80 and allocates the list (0x944e46 of 0x1e0 at +0xa7; when out of memory, the error box for line 0x147 and −1). 
 From the Japanese clubs (+0x53 = [0x9cf36c]) that have a division, into local vectors: those of [0x9cf678] (up to 100), those of [0x9cf674] (up to 30), those of [0x9cf670] (up to 30) and those of divisions other than J2 ([0x9cf768]) and J1 ([0x9cf65c]) (up to 6); if there are none of the latter, the last club of [0x9cf678] is moved from there to here. With fewer than 47, 2, 3 or 1 in each of them, the error box for line 0x178 and 0. 
 Each vector is sorted and shuffled (0x4afbd0 with 47, 2, 3 and 1 picks); the list takes the first 47, 2 and 3 (the last vector is not used), class 0; then the J2 clubs while they fit (class 0) and the J1 clubs while they fit, with class = last season's position (+0x5f), until the list is full; then qsort (0x522190) of the last 16 entries. 
 Returns 1 with the list full, otherwise 0.

Creates one group (a League_Stage with 4 teams) in [+0xc][`g`], frees the round table and returns the stage. \n The round table comes from virtual +0x3c (push 0; push &id; push &rodadas; push `g`; mov ecx, this -> thiscall, ret 0x10). The stage (0x944cf1(0xee) push; add esp, 4 -> cdecl; constructor League_Stage 0x68b100, thiscall, ret 0x58, 22 arguments: the cup, 4, the 4 teams, 1, +4, the round table, the rounds (word), 3, 1, 8, &{1, 2, 0, 0}, &{2, 0, 0, 0}, the year +0x40 (word), `g`, the id (word), +0x51, `a17`, 0, 0x28, −1, 0, 2; the original routine pushes the words and bytes with garbage in the high bytes, which the constructor does not read) goes into [+0xc][`g`]; the table is freed (0x9452ca). \n Returns the stage.

Describes one stage of virtual +0x3c (`create_schedule(fase, &rodadas, &extra, &é_liga)`). \n It holds the é_liga written (if requested), the rounds, the extra (only if the pointer is not null, when `extra_checa`), the table size, the error-box line when out of memory, the operations and the counter name. `None`: the stage returns 0 without writing anything.

Side-by-side comparer of create_round_table. \n The original routine runs with the caller's outputs, the copy with its own outputs that start with the same values, both from the same [0xb67a34]; the outputs and the bytes written to the two tables must be equal; the copy's table is freed (0x9452ca). \n In the stage without a table only the original runs (neither writes anything; the outputs may not even exist).

The 4 finalists of the Asian Cup Winners' Cup: the surviving entrants of the two zones' knockouts, with the 2nd and 3rd swapped. \n The survivors (+5 = 1 in the 6-byte table) of the first zone's knockout (the cup's table, +0xa7) and then those of the second (table +0xa7 of stage [+0xc][0]), up to 4 in total, both searches going up to the cup's +0x3e (signed word). The 2nd and 3rd swap places (the pairings: the brackets are the pairs of the list). \n Slots left over stay 0 (the original routine leaves them with whatever malloc returned).

Builds the knockout stage after the groups (qualifier list, round table, Cup_Stage) and draws round 0. 
 The same template is used in the Libertadores and the Merconorte, checked instruction by instruction: only the list size, the group stages, the knockout stage, the source file and the error-box lines change. 
 The list (0x944e46(4 × times): push; add esp, 4 -> cdecl; when out of memory, the error box `linha_sem_lista` and return) gets the first +0xbe of group 1 (in row order) and, from each group stage 0..`fases` − 1, the first +0xbe (positions 0, 1...). The round table comes from virtual +0x3c (push 0; push &id; push &rodadas; push `mata`; mov ecx, this -> thiscall, ret 0x10). The stage (0x944cf1(0xb2) push; add esp, 4 -> cdecl; Cup_Stage::Cup_Stage 0x522e00, thiscall, ret 0x3c: the cup, `times`, the list, the rounds, +4, the table, the year +0x40, `mata`, 2, the id, 0x14, 0, 0, 0 and no seeds; the original routine pushes the rounds, the id and the year with garbage in the high 16 bits, which the constructor does not read) goes into [+0xc][`mata`]; the list and the table are freed (0x9452ca). 
 Without a stage: the error box `linha_sem_fase`. With one: the draw of round 0 (0x51c410 Cup::draw_round: push 0; mov ecx, stage -> thiscall, ret 4). 
 The original routine's SEH frame only covers the constructor (no destructor).

Shared body of virtual +0x3c (`create_schedule(fase, &rodadas, &extra, &é_liga)`, thiscall, ret 0x10; the stage read as a signed byte) of the South American cups: group rounds below `limite`, knockout rounds at it, nothing above. 
 Below `limite` (−1 included), the groups: é_liga (if requested) = 1, rodadas = the number of group rounds, extra = stage + 0x3e9 (16 bits); the table of 0x41 bytes per round (0x944e46; when out of memory, the error box `linha_g` and returns 0) with the dates of `grupos`. 
 At stage `limite`, the knockout: é_liga = 0, rodadas = the size of `mata`, extra = 0; the table of 0x68 bytes per round (when out of memory, the error box `linha_m`), the rounds written by `eng_cc_cup_write_cup_round` with the cup's year +0x40 (signed) and the words of `a_mais` (round, offset, value). 
 Above `limite`: returns 0 without writing anything.

The positions that 0x586900 records, in the order of its calls to 0x4a2540: (index of the club in the sorted vector, position). 
 `mata` is the knockout round table (0x68 bytes per round, +0x1a the tie count) with `nm` rounds; the preliminaries come from [+0xa3] with +0x3c rounds. 
 1) The knockout, from the final backwards: in the final, those of the first pass get position 1 (the counter goes up with each one); in every round, each of the following ones gets the counter value from the start of the round (which goes up with each one). 
 2) The second group stage: 2 × (4 clubs with the counter; the counter goes up by 4). 3) The first group stage: 2 × (8 clubs; it goes up by 8). 
 4) The preliminaries, from the last to the first: each club of the round gets the counter value from the start of that round (it goes up with each one).
Sorts by reputation and shuffles the top band. \n Uses 0x4afbd0 comp_util_sort_and_shuffle_top_clubs (push how many; push the count; push list; add esp -> cdecl; draws at random).

Describes one stage of virtual +0x3c (`create_schedule(fase, &rodadas, &extra, &é_liga)`). \n It holds the é_liga written (if requested), the rounds, the extra (only if the pointer is not null, when `extra_checa`), the table size, the error-box line when out of memory, the common operations and the stage's own operations (the matches of each group) and the counter name. `None`: the stage returns 0 without writing anything.

Side-by-side comparer of the stage table builder. \n The original routine runs with the caller's outputs, the copy with its own outputs that start with the same values, both from the same [0xb67a34]; the outputs and the bytes written to the two tables must be equal; the copy's table is freed (0x9452ca). \n In the stage without a table only the original runs (neither writes anything; the outputs may not even exist).
The rehearsal of the comparer for one day's conflicts. The copy does not add anything (0x68d0d0 allocates the node and the copy of the match) and keeps, in order, the matches it would add.
Rehearsal mode of 0x5ae380 (the comparer). The copy stops at the decision, before touching the calendar.
The rehearsal of the news item. The copy builds the new news item here instead of putting it in the queue (and does not create the queue).

The calendar block for the year of match `f` (+0x28, word), walking the calendar chain from `fm`. \n This is the loop shared by 0x5ac7a0, 0x5ab230 and 0x5abc30: the next block (+0x112c) of another year is moved to the requested year (0x5aa2d0 set_year); with no next block, a new block (0x944cf1, 0x1184 bytes; 0x5a9cf0 with the year, the previous block and 0) joins the chain. \n Returns 0 if memory ran out (the chain keeps 0 at +0x112c, as in the original routine).

Second part of 0x5cbdf0: for each free nation in the sorted list, finds the first suitable later free nation and creates the international friendly; the rehearsal replays taped draws. 
 Each nation `a` of the sorted list (+0x34fa, count +0x34fe re-read on every pass) that is still free, belongs to one of the date's confederations and is not African on the African date, searches among the following free nations `b` for the first one that fits: a random draw out of 500 (0x90cfc0, before the filters on `b`), `b` on the date and not African, one of the two with +0x88 ≥ 5, the pair not banned (0x5cc3e0), one more draw out of 1000 if the continent (+0x71) is the same, the sum above 400 and `b` not yet in the list of `a`'s position (+0x34f6, by position; the cursor goes back to the start). 
 Once found: the venue drawn at random (0x90cfc0 out of 2), the senior national teams (0x53b3d0, `b` first) and the friendly (0x5c6f00 with the date +3); once created, the forced answer (0x5c5f40 with 1), both marked and each one in the list of the other's position (`b` in `a`'s, then `a` in `b`'s; the 4 bytes of the record, the id). Created or not, the next `a`. 
 In the rehearsal the friendly is not created: what the original routine did counts (the id of `b` appeared in the list of `a`'s position), the draws come from the tape and, after the venue, the rest continues (from the next `a`) at the first draw out of 500 on the tape (or at the end) that fits: the draws inside the friendly's routines are left behind. 
 Starts at nation `i0`.

Writes the host and second host of entry `e` for bid `k` (the default when `k` < 0); returns how many are valid (≠ −1). \n The entries are 0x22-byte records: +0 competition id, +4 year, +6 the default host and the second one (+0xa), +6 + 8 × k the bids k = 0..2 (host and second host), +0x1e the chosen one (0..2; −3 the fixed default, −1 voting open, −2 voting still closed), +0x1f the day of the year of the decisions, +0x21 the interval in years.

Virtual +0x44 of a national-team tournament with groups and knockout (the African Nations Cup and the Copa América): writes the qualification, elimination and final-placing records by outcome and stage; returns 0. 
 `fase` (signed byte) below `grupos` is the group stage: 6, qualification (0x86bdd0: stage 0, round 0x78, weight 0x19); 0xfe, non-qualification (0x86c1d0: stage 0x41c, weight 0x19), which ends the call-ups. 
 At stage `grupos` (the knockout, stage [+0xc][grupos]): 0, qualification with the match's stage +0x32, the +0x6f of the match's round (+0x34) in the stage's round table (+0xa3, 0x68 bytes) and the weight 0x4bf850(0x28, 0x64, round, 3); 0xff, elimination (0x86c000) with +0x32, +0x30 and the same weight; 1, 2 and 3, the champion, runner-up and third-place records. 
 Returns 0.

`EuroChampQual::set_up_rules()` (0x57e8f0, thiscall, ret 0, euro_champ_qual.cpp; virtual +0x8c, from the constructor in 2001-000; SEH frame for the local Date, no destructor): sets points, rounds, tie-breakers, qualification places and the draw date, and builds the round table; returns 1. 
 3 points for a win (+0xc2) and 1 for a draw (+0xc3), +0x4a = 3, two rounds (+0x3c = 2, word), match category 0xa (+0xc4), +0x43 = 2, tie-breakers 1, 2, 4, 5 (+0xc5..+0xc8), one direct place (+0xbe = 1) and one play-off place (+0xbf = 1), no relegation (+0xc0 = +0xc1 = 0), +0x49 = 7, +0xa7 = 0xffff (word). 
 The draw date (+0xb6, the day of the year) = Date(10, 2, year +0x40, 5) (0x549f70: push 5; push year; push 2; push 0xa; lea ecx, local -> thiscall, ret 0x10: 10 March moved to the Friday [inference]); +0xb8 = 0 (word); the round table from virtual +0x3c (push 0; push &+0x3a; push &+0xa9; push −1; mov ecx -> thiscall, ret 0x10) at +0xba. 
 Returns 1.

Builds the round table of tournament phase `f`, or returns 0 without it. \n It writes the outputs, the table (0x944e46; when out of memory, the error box `linha` of source file `arquivo` and 0) and the operations in order. The cup year (+0x40) goes as clean 16 bits to 0x68a160 (the original routine pushes the register with garbage in the high 16 bits; 0x68a160 only uses the word) and signed to the cup routines.

Side-by-side comparer for a phase table. \n The original routine runs with the caller's outputs, the copy with its own outputs that start with the same values, both from the same [0xb67a34]; the outputs and the bytes written to the two tables must be equal; the copy's table is freed (0x9452ca). \n In the stage without a table only the original runs (neither writes anything; the outputs may not even exist).

The league TV date table entry (0x41 bytes at [+0xba], count +0xa9) for a date, found by bsearch as in 0x685640. \n None when there are no entries, when the date is after the last one (year +2 + the league's +0x40, unsigned; day +0 signed), when the search does not find the entry (0x946464: push 0x685cf0; push 0x41; push count; push table; push &key; add esp, 0x14 -> cdecl bsearch; the key is the day and the year minus the league's) or when the first slot is empty (+0xb = 0xff).

Calls the league's virtual +0x40 (League::announce_team_status: thiscall(league, club, situation, stage, 0, 0), ret 0x14) with the club of row `i`. \n `alto` = the upper bits of the register that the original routine pushes with the stage (+0x44) in the low byte (the row pointer or the clauses' return value: reproduced). In the rehearsal the recorded tape is replayed.

League table rows: 0x3b bytes. \n +0 club, +4 position, +5 head-to-head records of 14 bytes, +9 position history, +0x11/+0x1f/+0x2d the totals, home and away, +0x37 status, +0x38 mark, +0x39, +0x3a clubs.

Comparer of the play-off creation: runs only the original routine and then checks the new stage against the plan. \n Only the original runs (it allocates the list, the table and the stage and draws the round), with the plan made beforehand: the clubs of the rows. \n Afterwards, the stage in the first slot must exist, with +0x3e = 4, +4 = the league's +4 and the first 4 clubs of its list (+0xa7, 6 bytes) equal to those of the plan (as a set: the round draw may reorder them), and +0x30 = 0.

The season turnovers of the other fourteen competitions in Brazil, in the original routine's order. \n Série B, Série C and the twelve state leagues (Baiano, Centro-Oeste, Gaúcho, Goiano, Mineiro, Norte, Nordeste, Paranaense, Pernambucano, Carioca, Catarinense and Paulista: the id globals 0x9cf9e0, 0x9cf9ac, 0x9cf9c0, 0x9cf998, 0x9cf9c8, 0x9cf9b4, 0x9cf9d4, 0x9cf994, 0x9cf9a4, 0x9cf9d0, 0x9cf9bc, 0x9cf9dc, 0x9cf9b0, 0x9cf9e4).

Comparer of the Série A and Série B table creation: runs only the original routine, then checks +0x3e, the return value and the table rows against the planned clubs. \n The original allocates the table (and in Série A pays the TV money with a news item), so only it runs. The plan, made beforehand: the division's clubs in database order (up to `n`). \n Afterwards: +0x3e = `n`, the return value = 1 if the plan filled up (otherwise 0) and the table rows (+0 the club, 0x3b bytes) hold the planned clubs, in order.

Shared season turnover of the state leagues (`start_new_season`, slot 3, +0x08): frees the table, lists and stages, archives the statistics, advances the year, rebuilds rules, table and fixtures and renews the officials. 
 The same template is used in the nine round-robin state leagues with a knockout; only the source file, the error-box lines and the table routine change, checked instruction by instruction. 
 +0x4c = 0 and the table freed (League::free_table 0x687970, thiscall(this, 0), ret 4); the list at +0xba freed (free 0x9452ca) and zeroed; with statistics (+8), Comp_Stats::archive_season_and_reset (0x4a1c50, thiscall(+8, 1), ret 4); with the current stage ≥ 0, the existing stages 0..=+0x30 destroyed (virtual 0, the destructor with 1: frees); the year (+0x40, word) goes up by one (`ano`; the counter `ramo`) and +0x30 = −1. 
 Then, each with its own error box if it returns 0: the season rules (virtual +0x8c, set_up_rules), the table with the state league's clubs (`tabela`, thiscall, ret 0), the fixtures (League::create_fixtures 0x6835c0, thiscall, ret 0) and the table order (League::sort_table 0x6827d0, thiscall(this, 0), ret 4). 
 Finally the predicted positions (virtual +0x5c) and the renewal of the state league's referees (OfficialsManager::renew_officials 0x79cee0, thiscall([0xb74340], +4), ret 4), whose eax it returns.

Raises a club's attendance (+0x73) to a floor that rises with reputation `r` and factor `f`, and raises the record (+0x7b) with it. \n The floor (from the branches that push attendance up): with r < 5, 250 × r × f; otherwise 750 × (r − 4) × f + 1000 (the original routine compares with the integer part + 1000 and writes the value with 1000 added before truncation). \n Below it, attendance goes up to it and the record (+0x7b) rises up to it.

Comparer of the three state league tables: runs only the original routine, then checks `n`, the return value and the row clubs against the planned clubs. \n The original allocates the table (it cannot run twice), so only it runs. Comparer of the weekly finance events: the copy in rehearsal mode (no news item and no budget) and the original routine from the same state (finance record and random draws). \n With no event: everything equal, including the random draws. Shared body of the two French table creations: `n` clubs (+0x3e), allocates the table and fills the rows from the list `clubes`, marking clubs whose competition is in `marcadas`; returns whether it filled up. \n +0x3e = `n`, the table (malloc 0x944e46 of n × 0x3b; when out of memory: the error box of source file `arquivo` at line `linha` and 0) and the `n` clubs of the list `clubes`, in order, each in the next row (League::init_table_row 0x687430: thiscall(league, row, club, mark, 0), ret 0x10), with mark 1 on the clubs whose competition (+0x57, the id at +0) is one of `marcadas`. \n Returns whether it filled up (the row count = +0x3e).

Shared body of the two set_up_fixed_fixtures (thiscall, ret 0, SEH frame only for the vector constructor): allocates the fixed fixtures vector at +0xea, sets each fixture from the table by club names and drops the vector if any club was not found.

 Then each fixture of `tabela`, in order, in its place in the vector (fixed_fixture_set_by_club_names 0x68aff0: push the 6th (away, via the map); push the 5th (home); push year; push month (0 = January); push day; push league; mov ecx, [+0xea] + 16 × k -> thiscall, ret 0x18: the date and the clubs found by name, −1 at +8/+0xc if not found). 
 Finally, if any of the n fixtures was left with a club not found (+8 or +0xc = −1), the vector is destroyed (`eh vector destructor iterator` 0x9462bb: push 0x5a53c0; push count; push 0x10; push vector -> stdcall, ret 0x10; operator delete 0x944c94 of the block: push; add esp, 4 -> cdecl) and +0xea = 0: the league goes back to the randomly drawn calendar.
The second division: 38 rounds from 31 July to 20 May; 18 rounds with one TV slot (day 5, half 1, 1 match).

League::init_table_row (0x687430: thiscall(league, row, club, 0, 0), ret 0x10) for row (k + `girar`) % n with the club. \n `girar` is 0 (the original: row k); it exists only for each league's mutations. Simplification: the original routine pushes the row in eax with spare upper bits; 0x687430 only reads the byte.

Sets the dates and match slots of rounds `primeira`.. of table `t`, in the original routine's order. \n For each round, the date (0x68a160: push 0; push year; push code; push week; push years; push month; push day; push i; push t; add esp -> cdecl: value 0) and the slots (0x68a1c0: push 0; push c; push b; push a; push j; push i; push t; add esp -> cdecl, value 0).

Sets the dates and match slots of rounds `primeira`.. of table `t`, in the original routine's order. \n For each round, the date (0x68a160: push 0; push year; push code; push week; push years; push month; push day; push i; push t; add esp -> cdecl: value 0) and the slots (0x68a1c0: push 0; push c; push b; push a; push j; push i; push t; add esp -> cdecl, value 0).

Describes one round of the 0x41-byte table. \n It holds the date (day, month 0..11, years to add to the league year +0x40, the weekday the date is moved to), the code of byte +4 ([inference] the half of the season) and the TV slots in order (weekday, half, how many matches; the list ends with −1).

Creates the stage of one of the other MLS divisions (`create_second_division_stage` and `create_third_division_stage`): club vector, round table, League_Stage, stored in slot k with the division code. 
 Same template in both, checked instruction by instruction: only the division code, slot k, the error boxes' source file and the lines change. 
 1) A vector of +0x3e clubs (malloc 0x944e46 of 4 × +0x3e; when out of memory: the error box for line `linhas[0]` and return) with the clubs of the competition with `codigo`, in database order (i32 counter), while there are slots left. 
 2) The round table from virtual +0x3c (create_round_table: thiscall(this, −3, &rodadas, &extra, 0), ret 0x10). 
 3) The stage: operator new 0x944cf1(0xee) and the League_Stage constructor 0x68b100 (thiscall, ret 0x58, 22 arguments, in the original routine's order: the league, +0x3e (word), the vector, +0x3c (word, the rounds), +4, the round table, the rounds (word), the points +0xc2 (`pv`) and +0xc3, the category +0xc4, &+0xc5, &+0xbe (the league's places), the year +0x40 (word), k, the extra (word), +0x51, 1, +0xab (word), +0xd9 (word), +0xa7 (word), 0, 2; the copy passes clean values).  4) [+0xc][k] = the stage; the vector and the round table freed (free 0x9452ca, in that order). Without a stage: the error box for line `linhas[1]`. With one: +0x30 = `atual` (the original writes k) and the stage's +0x3a = the division code.

The keys of the 32 nations of the real 2002 draw (the g_key_nation_* globals, index into the nation table [0xae23a8], 0x122 bytes each), in the order in which the original routine writes them to the list: groups A to H, four per group.

Comparer for `awol_post_missed_training_news` (comparison mode: see the header of motor.rs). \n The original routine builds the news item and delivers it (it allocates in the inbox), so only it runs, with the random draws traced; then the copy in rehearsal mode redoes the path with the draws from the tape, without delivering. \n It checks that the rehearsal's draws are the start of the original's tape (the rest belongs to the delivery) with the same n, and records the destination (the original does not expose it).

Comparer for `update_transfer_fee_records` (comparison mode: see the header of motor.rs). \n The original routine puts items in the news queue (it reallocates) and the liking draws at random, so: the plan first (the four records created in the same order as the original, and the expected paid and received records); the original runs; it fetches the records again (the vector may have been reallocated) and checks the values and the club of each record and [0xae1080].

Comparer for `record_team_progress` (comparison mode: see the header of motor.rs). \n Comparer of 0x521b30: side by side on the 3 progress bytes (+0x73..+0x75) of the club's record in the cup's Comp_Stats (+8, found by 0x4a4850: push club; ecx = the statistics; thiscall, ret 4), which +0x68 writes. The versions that pass it on to another competition write outside that region (then the comparison only checks that nothing changed in it). \n Without statistics, without a club or without a record: only the original.

Comparer for `move_round_fixtures_to_set_dates` (comparison mode: see the header of motor.rs). 
 Comparer of 0x51ebe0: only the original routine runs (the matches leave the calendar and come back through 0x5aa680, which allocates, and the news items go to the managers). 
 The plan, made beforehand: the cup's matches on the date and slice (0x5abd90 into a temporary list), in list order; each one of the league's type takes the next slot (every 7 bytes, up to 0x38 and up to the first 0xff), and the slot of the one on the round's date becomes 0xff; the other slots do not change. 
 Without the cup in [0xadadfc] afterwards: nothing to check.

Comparer for `con_merc_cup_select_invited_clubs` (comparison mode: see the header of motor.rs). \n Side by side: +0xf2, [0xb67a34] and the random generator's state, starting from the same state (the copy draws without counting); the original routine leaves its list at +0xee, the copy builds its own, compared over the 16 slots and freed. \n The draws of the nations' lists stay on each one's stack: only the final list and the random generator count.

Comparer for `draw_phase2_groups` (comparison mode: see the header of motor.rs). \n Only the original routine runs (it draws, pays prize money, allocates the stages and sends news; and it calls itself again), checking the plan: on the outer call (attempt 0), stages 8..11 exist, +0x30 = 11 and the clubs of their tables (+0xb1, 0x3b-byte rows) are the 16 qualified clubs.

Comparer for `european_cup_create_round_table` (comparison mode: see the header of motor.rs). \n Side by side in the group stages: the original routine with the caller's outputs, the copy with its own outputs, from the same [0xb67a34]; the outputs and the bytes written to the two tables must be equal (the copy's is freed). \n The preliminaries and the knockout: only the original.

Comparer for `find_fixture_clashes` (comparison mode: see the header of motor.rs). \n The comparer of one match's conflicts: the original routine and the copy, each with its own new list, from the same state (the original does not change the match: it only creates the list and moves the cursors of the day lists, which both redo). \n It checks the return value (list or 0), the output and the matches of the two lists (0x4f bytes each, in order), and destroys and frees the copy's list as the calendar does (0x68d040, 0x944c94).

Comparer for `arrange_international_friendlies` (comparison mode: see the header of motor.rs). 
 The original routine creates friendlies (0x5c6f00, 0x5c5f40), adds to the lists (0x68d0d0) and draws at random, so only it runs, with the plan in rehearsal mode. The first part of the rehearsal runs before it (afterwards the calendar would already have the new friendlies); the second part, after it, uses the tape of the draws it made (rng::rastrear: n and the answer, including those inside the friendly's routines) and decides each friendly by what the original did. 
 It checks the draw sequence (the rehearsal's draws are the original's, except those inside the friendly's routines, and the tape ends at the same point) and, nation list by nation list, that the original's new items are the ones the rehearsal would add. 
 (Side by side by the random generator's state did not work: 0x5c6f00 and 0x5c5f40 draw internally in the original and the rehearsal does not call them.)

Comparer for `update_international_friendlies` (comparison mode: see the header of motor.rs). \n On the first day of the year (the lists are emptied, freeing memory) and when there are friendlies to arrange (0x5cbdf0 creates matches and draws at random), only the original routine runs, checking the plan: the day set at +0x34f4. \n On the other days, side by side on the set day and the static dates.

Comparer for `move_fixtures_for_tv` (comparison mode: see the header of motor.rs). \n Comparer of 0x685640: only the original routine runs (the matches leave the calendar and come back through 0x5aa680, which allocates, the ratings draw at random and the news items go to the managers). \n The plan, made beforehand: from the date's entry, the league's matches on its day and slice (0x5abd90 into a temporary list) and the valid slots (slice 0..2) before the first empty one; each valid slot takes one match while the list has any (every rating gets past the initial −1), and the slot becomes 0xff: the 0xff slots of the block after the original are min(valid slots, matches).

Comparer for `copy_table` (comparison mode: see the header of motor.rs). \n It allocates (it cannot run twice), so only the original routine runs, with the full plan checked afterwards: the expected +0xa7 (computed beforehand) and the returned copy equal to the table, row by row (except the pointers of the new vectors), with the head-to-head and form vectors equal to the table's.

Comparer for `create_finals_series_stage` (comparison mode: see the header of motor.rs). \n The finals series comparer: only the original routine runs (it allocates the round table and the stage and sends the news item), with the plan made beforehand: the top six of the table. \n Afterwards, return value 1, the stage in slot 0 with +0x3e = 6, +4 = the league's +4 and the six in its table (+0xb1, as a set), and +0x30 = 0.

Comparer for `bra_nat_third_set_predicted_positions` (comparison mode: see the header of motor.rs). \n The predicted positions comparer: only the original routine runs (0x4a2540 adds the record of a club that has none; it cannot run twice), with the plan made beforehand: the list of the 56 sorted by the same qsort on a copy. \n Afterwards, the league's list in the same order and the position (+0x72 of the record found by 0x4a4850) of each club.

Comparer for `bra_reg_minas_gerais_advance_stage` (comparison mode: see the header of motor.rs). \n The next-stage comparer: only the original routine runs (simplification: on reaching 2 it builds the final, which allocates and draws at random; it cannot run twice), checking the plan: on the last stage, +0x30 unchanged; otherwise +0x30 + 1, or, on reaching 2, 2 (with a final) or 1 (the same champion in both halves, which the final writes).

Comparer for `bra_reg_parana_create_final_stage` (comparison mode: see the header of motor.rs). \n The final's comparer: only the original routine runs (it allocates the list, the table and the stage and draws the round), checking the plan made beforehand: the champions of the two halves. \n Same club in both: +0x30 = 1, +0x2c = 2 and status 5 on the first row of each half and on its row of the league table. Different: the stage in the third slot exists, with +0x3e = 2, +4 = the league's +4 and the two champions in its list (+0xa7, 6 bytes; as a set: the round draw may reorder them), and +0x30 = 2.

Comparer for `bra_reg_rio_create_final_stage` (comparison mode: see the header of motor.rs). \n The final's comparer: only the original routine runs (it allocates the list, the table and the stage and draws the round), checking the plan made beforehand: the champions of the two halves. \n Same club in both: +0x30 = 1, +0x2c = 2 and status 5 on the first row of each half and on its row of the league table. Different: the stage in the third slot exists, with +0x3e = 2, +4 = the league's +4 and the two champions in its list (+0xa7, 6 bytes; as a set: the round draw may reorder them), and +0x30 = 2.

Comparer for `ita_ser_c2a_update_staff_records_for_status` (comparison mode: see the header of motor.rs). \n Comparer of 0x654180: the records go to the people's history and change reputations and morale (they cannot run twice), so only the original routine runs. \n The plan, made beforehand, in stages 0 and 1: the club's first row with status 1, 2 or 0xff decides the +0x37 that the routine writes (stage 0: 0 with 1, 0xfe with 2/0xff; stage 1: 0xfe with 1, 3 with 2/0xff); afterwards the row must be like that. Comparer for `usa_mls_create_playoff_stage` (comparison mode: see the header of motor.rs). \n The play-off comparer: only the original routine runs (it allocates the list, the table and the stage and draws the round), with the plan made beforehand by the copy of the selection (the same records and the same qsort): the stage in the third slot exists, with +0x3e = 8, +4 = the league's +4 and the eight in its list (+0xa7, 6 bytes; as a set).

Comparer for `usa_mls_set_predicted_positions` (comparison mode: see the header of motor.rs). \n The predicted positions comparer: only the original routine runs (simplification: 0x4a2540 adds the record of a club that has none; it cannot run twice), with the plan made beforehand: the twelve clubs of the three tables, each block sorted by the same qsort on a copy; afterwards, the position (+0x72 of the record found by 0x4a4850) of each one.

Comparer for `build_venue_list` (comparison mode: see the header of motor.rs). \n Side by side by hand: the original routine on the caller's object, the copy on a scratch object with the same 0x20 bytes as before and the old list zeroed (the original has already released it); the fields (except the pointer +0xc) and the lists must be equal (the scratch object's list is released). \n Without the HostCountry (the error box): only the original.

Comparer for `database_player_initialisation` (comparison mode: see the header of motor.rs). \n Comparer of 0x535a80: original routine and copy side by side over the database it writes (whole persons, players and non-players, the 79-byte-per-person table at [0xae2d0c]), [0x9b59b4], the flags 0x9b59b8/9 and the four global template vectors, the text at 0xde1f64, the stored date of 0x54cab0 and the random generator's state (the copy without counting draws). \n Without persons (error box and end): only the original.

Comparer for `apply_match_effects` (comparison mode: see the header of motor.rs). \n Side by side on the random generator's state, on the cursor of the knocks list and on the recovery (+0xa, 4 bytes, of the 31-byte record at [this]) of each person in the slots. \n A match with a knock that reaches the injury type: only the original routine (the new injury allocates and sends the news item; the severity of the first knock may be stack residue).

Comparer for `add_illness_outbreak` (comparison mode: see the header of motor.rs). \n The original routine draws at random, allocates and reorders: the plan first (the draws and the selection, with the random generator's state saved and restored); then the original runs. \n It checks the same random generator state and, if the outbreak was added, the count +1 and the outbreak (date, type, club, match) in the vector; otherwise the count unchanged.

Comparer: side by side from the same state of the club's board record, of the contract stored at [0xae1080] and of the random generator; the return value and all of these must match (the CRT rand, only without the clock seed). \n When buying, the first thing both do is the injury (0x62ed70), which first brings the player's injury up to date (0x62c680: once a day, it may draw at random and writes the date to the record); the original routine, running first, brought it up to date and the copy then skipped a draw (one draw fewer). \n The comparer performs that same update beforehand (the game's own, at the same point: nothing before it draws), and both start from the injury already up to date.

Comparer for `match_screens_draw_live_league_table` (comparison mode: see the header of motor.rs). \n The live table is genuinely compared through the display list, together with the league (0xee bytes: [+0xad]) and its table ([+0xb1], 59 bytes per club), which the routine reorders. The local copies are born and die inside it. \n Without a league or without parameter 0xe ("Error" box): only the original routine.

Comparer for `painel_pela_lista` (comparison mode: see the header of motor.rs). \n The three panels are genuinely compared: both draw from the same state, and the screen manager, the current screen's `Display`, the parameter block with the marks 0xb6b7a8/ac/b0 and the text 0xde1f64 must come out equal. \n The list (0x55fba0) also writes into a network buffer ([0xae2908] at position [0xae290c]): the position is included in the regions (it is reset so the second run writes to the same place, and the size written is compared); the contents of that buffer are not.

Comparer for `send_club_international_report_news` (comparison mode: see the header of motor.rs). \n Comparer of 0x7706c0: the original routine delivers the news items (it allocates in the inboxes), so only it runs, with the random draws traced and the squad saved beforehand. \n Then the squad is put back as it was, the copy redoes the work in rehearsal mode (draws from the tape, without delivering) and the squad must come out equal to the original's, with the rehearsal's draws equal to the tape's (same n, all used).

Comparer for `record_international_result` (comparison mode: see the header of motor.rs). \n The rehearsal (the copy without the ranking, the first call-up, the transfer record and the news item, which allocate, go to the file or write elsewhere) and the original routine from the same state, checked over the regions the routine writes on its own (caps_update_regions). \n Outside a match between national teams: only the original.

Comparer: byte +0x6b of the record, the under-21 slots and their persons (+0x24 to +0x5e). \n The copy's 0x896c60 no longer finds the persons that the original routine has already removed (it stays outside the regions, as in 0x7762f0). \n Null under-21 team: only the original.

Comparer for `record_club_call_ups` (comparison mode: see the header of motor.rs). \n Side by side on the team's squad (50 slots) and, for each club of the squad that counts, on the record (6 bytes) and on the whole entries vector (capacity × 9). \n When some vector may grow (0x945667 releases the old one; it cannot run twice): only the original routine, then checking the squad sorted by club (the same qsort on a copy, done beforehand).

Comparer for `player_search_record_scouted_club_match` (comparison mode: see the header of motor.rs). \n Comparer of 0x7bd310: side by side over the 50 slots (the whole record). \n With the masks on and the club's manager human, 0x5b09d0 writes what is known about the player and draws at random: then only the original routine runs (simplification: the case of a human scouting their own club; the automatic career never reaches this routine).

Comparer for `create_stats` (comparison mode: see the header of motor.rs). \n The original routine reallocates the vector, so only it runs; beforehand, the plan (the index the player will get, the count and the free ones afterwards); afterwards, the returned record, the index in the slot, the count, the free ones and the record zeroed when it is new. \n Simplification: the error cases and running out of memory only in the original, unchecked.

Comparer for `scout_manager_daily_update` (comparison mode: see the header of motor.rs). \n Comparer of 0x7f8750: the reports draw at random and allocate and the searches change the human players' lists, so only the original routine runs. \n Beforehand, the copy in rehearsal mode prunes a copy of the requests (without the reports) and puts them in the original's order; the requests the original leaves (count and the 0x11 bytes of each) must be those.

Comparer for `record_manager_job_change` (comparison mode: see the header of motor.rs). \n A comparer in rehearsal mode: the manager's record created beforehand (0x86f5b0, as the original routine would do on the two paths that need it), the copy without the histories and the original from the same state (the record, 0xd2 bytes, and the static date of 0x54cdb0). \n Nulls: only the original.

Comparer for `add_year_award_record` (comparison mode: see the header of motor.rs). \n The manager side by side through his points record (created beforehand by 0x86f5b0, as the original routine would do; the copy without the history entry in the file). \n The player draws at random, renews the contract and sends a news item (it cannot run twice): only the original. Without a person or without an award (the error box): only the original.

Comparer: side by side on the random generator's state, on [0xae1080], on the training entry (6 bytes), on the player sheet (+0xf..+0x41, what 0x8b2be0 writes) and on the load of the fitness sheet (31 bytes per player at [[0xb63d28]], +0x1e), with the copy's draws not counted. \n Only the original routine: the error cases and the player with position training (0x8b4b20 before running), because there 0x8b4450, the contract mark (0x867700) and 0x5885c0 write outside these regions.

Comparer for `pay_next_sale_percentage` (comparison mode: see the header of motor.rs). \n Comparer of 0x8cb0f0: the copy in rehearsal mode (without the news item and without the club totals) and the original routine from the same state, side by side on the two clubs' finances, on [0xae1080] and on the random generator (0x4d0c60 may draw). \n When paid (the original's news item and totals may rewrite [0xae1080]), only the finances and the return value.

Comparer for `unsettle_player_after_bid` (comparison mode: see the header of motor.rs). \n The copy in rehearsal mode and the original routine from the same state (the offer, [0xae1080] and the random generator). \n Without reaching the complaint (almost always), everything equal; when it is reached, only the original (the complaint, the walkout and the dislikes cannot run twice and the original draws more).

Comparer for `fill_vacated_staff_job` (comparison mode: see the header of motor.rs). \n The copy's choice first; with nobody, only the original routine. \n With a person, original and copy side by side on the club (0x245 bytes) and on the person (0x6e), which is everything 0x53bd10 writes: it may refuse (home occupied, the human players' range; it happens with more leagues) or write to the national team (+0x24), and the person does not stay at +0x39.

Shows the contract_manager.cpp "Error" message box for source line `linha`, as the original routine does; the game continues. \n The text is "v%s %s.%s %d" at 0xae24d0 (0x944cff splits the path 0x9a8190, 0x90d130 the version; the original does not pop its arguments, which are the rest of the format), then the box 0x5e8290 and [0xb67a34] = 0.

The reminder dates (type 2) that a type-1 decision date gets before it, from the contract morale; returns up to two dates and the count. \n With a player record (+0x61), L = contract morale (+0x44) + 100 (8 bits; the contract via the table [0xae2d0c], as 0x4cf5a0 inline: without a contract the original routine reads address 0x44 and crashes, as here); L ≤ 0x50 no reminder; L > 0x96 one reminder L × 90 / 200 days before; and one L / 4 days before (without a player record, L = 100). \n The dates come from Date::sub_days (0x54c8e0), in the original's order.

The texts of job roles 0..0x11 of 0x53ad00 (code immediates, through the addresses in the exe): short lowercase, short uppercase, full lowercase, full uppercase and the gender with language 4 (0: not written). \n The short ones use the empty text 0xad9c64 ("<%s - COMMENT - short name>"); of the full ones, only the player's (11). Role 14 does not exist (0).
The names of the 12 manager attributes (abbreviated, full) of 0x543b10, through the addresses of the texts in the exe. The abbreviated 8th (man management) is a format with the text of [0xad9c64].

Counts how many of the 50 squad members (+0xd7) count for the three squad-strength queries by the /65 limit. \n A member counts when: non-null person with a player record (+0x61) of `posicao`, no serious injury (INJURY 0x62c400 on [0xb63d28] ≠ 2), id (+0) < [0xae2364] (signed) and current ability (+5 of the player, signed short) above `limite`. \n The order of the tests is the original routine's (0x62c400 is only called for those of the position). 8-bit counter (at most 50).

Counts how many of the 50 squad members (+0xd7) are natural at position `posicao` and good enough for the club's reputation. \n A member counts when: person with a player record (+0x61) at `posicao` (byte = 20), no serious injury (INJURY 0x62c400 on [0xb63d28] ≠ 2), id (+0) < [0xae2364] (signed), current ability (+5, signed short) above reputation/75 + 25 (from 40 to 135) and `atributo` (signed byte) above reputation/500 + 5 (at most `teto`). Reputation: the club's +0x80, signed short. \n In the original routine's order. 8-bit counter (at most 50).
Comparer note: the `realloc` cannot be undone (growing twice would leave the table with 2n extra rows).

Competition record (107 bytes) in club_comp.dat / nation_comp.dat version 1 (104 in the file): `(deslocamento, tamanho, quantos)` in file order. \n Gaps at +0x37 and +0x52; size 0 = the reputation in one byte, u16 at +0x69.

Comparer: with `fread` (use_zip = 0), the original routine reads, the file is rewound (`fseek` 0x946a22 to the position from `ftell` 0x946aae) and the Rust routine reads again; it compares the records, the answer and where the file stopped.
The fixed colours (index.cpp keys at 0x9cf178..0x9cf1fc, ids) and the family of each one, in the order of the comparisons in 0x540520.
The nation that lends names to each language group (nation +0x77, 1..32): jump tables 0x53a060 and 0x53a528 (identical). Group 17 (0) draws at random between [0x9cf484] and [0x9cf404].

For a nation with few names, picks a nation of the same language group with enough names; returns (count, first row) or None to draw from the whole table. \n This is the shared stretch of 0x539c60 (0x539df0..) and 0x53a1b0 (0x53a2be..) for a nation with up to 100 names and a language group: the group's nation (table) if it has ≥ random(20) + 15 names in `conta`; otherwise up to 40 randomly drawn nations ([0xae2350], 0x122 bytes each at [0xae23a8]) until one of the same group with more than 5 first names (+0x18, in both cases) is found. \n Returns (how many in `conta`, first in `inicio`) if the chosen nation has ≥ 5 names; otherwise `None` (draw from the whole table).

What 0x556570 is going to do, read beforehand (the list of held bans loses and frees its items): the contract and the club, the person's held items (the slot and the 5 bytes) and, after them, the slots 0..2 not restored that the club does not cover.
The rehearsal of the news items: the copy stops at the point where it would build the news item (which draws at random and goes to the managers' inboxes).

The 42735-byte record of the human manager `pessoa`, or of the current human when null; None when the original routine shows its error box. \n With a null `pessoa`, it is the network player of the current human's slot, [0xb74c26 + 0x300 × slot]. The humans are the last 16 persons: index = id − ([0xae2364] − 16), valid from 0 to [manager+4] − 1.
The club competition keys of index.cpp (0x60efd0), in code order: (long name text, global that receives the row), in 3 chains; (0, global) = one more global written in the same assignment.

The injury names of player_setup.cfg (the comparison, the characters compared, the text in .rdata and the type), in the original routine's order. The last one, ARTHRITIS (8 characters, 0xa6b3a8), gives 0x4c, and none gives 0x4b.

The comparer's rehearsal: the copy runs without delivering the news item (0x786090, which allocates) and stops before the walkout (0x419840, which adds to the list and sends a news item), keeping the decision.
What the copy left in the regions of the training phase, waiting for the original routine to reach the comeback news items (0x62e010).

The person's injury status from the age of the current injury: 2 injured, 1 regaining fitness, 0 fit. \n The current injury is the index at [this] + id × 31 + 0xe (−1 without an injury). The difference from the game date to the injury date (+0x20 of the 48-byte record at [this+4], 0x54cc30) in years × 365 + days: below +0x2a, 2 (injured); below +0x28, 1 (regaining fitness); otherwise 0.
The World Cup competition ids: the finals and the six qualifying competitions (Europe [0x9cf780], Africa, Asia, CONCACAF, Oceania, South America).

The list node (14 bytes: +0 the item, +4 the size as a signed word, +6 the next, +0xa the previous) whose item has the same bytes as `dado`, starting from the head (+2); 0 if none. \n The size is used as in the original routine (movsx into the ecx of repe cmpsb): 0 counts as equal (the repe does not run and ZF comes from the earlier xor).

The comparer's rehearsal: the copy runs without delivering the news item (deliveries copy the news item into the human managers' inboxes, allocate and may trigger the automatic reply) and keeps the reach it would have (+0xde: 4 everyone, 2 those of the country, 1 those of the division; 0 none) and the news item built.

Body of 0x690890 without the calls: person `pessoa` (fields in `s`) leaves his post at club `clube` (fields in `c`), by role. 
 `s` and `c` are the records themselves in the copy and copies of them in the comparer's plan. 
 By role at the club (+0x3d, table 0x690af8): 1 chairman (+0xbf), 2 directors (+0xc3, 3), 5 manager (+0xcf, if it is him), 6 assistant (+0xd3), 8 coaches (+0x19f, 5), 9 scouts (+0x1b3, 7), 10 physios (+0x1cf, 3): the slot zeroed and +0x39 = 0; 12, 13, 15 (player-manager, player-assistant, player-coach): the slot zeroed and role 0xb (stays at the club); others: +0x39 = 0 only if the low byte of the person pointer is 0 (the original routine's `[esp+0x10]`). 
 At the national team (+0x24, role +0x28, table 0x690b34) the same with +0x24, without the manager check, and the other roles leave.

`0x6d1210` (ret 4, match_eng.cpp) with the calls that change things outside the engine injected: applies the pending incidents (+0x1a3 entries from +0xb1): referee punishment, cards, commentary, team anger, sendings-off and the AI's resulting team changes. 
 The injected calls: 0x6d6f70 commentary; inside 0x6cda20 and at the end, 0x6e1aa0/0x6e1090 of the staff and 0x897760 of the captain. 
 On the 1st call (+0x8eb4 = 0) it only prepares `primeiro` (0x716630 with 0) and sets +0x8eb4 = 1 if there are pending ones. 
 Then it applies each of the +0x1a3 pending incidents (11 bytes from +0xb1: player, other, severity, code, x): the referee's punishment (0x6ea4e0, type 1) gives the card; 2 comments 0x1ff9, 3 and 4 (sending-off) comment 0x1ff7/0x1ff8 and mark +0x1cb of the side (goalkeeper: table 1); without a card, severity above random(7) + 2 with the player on the pitch comments 0x210a. When commenting, 0x20f5 (random(severity) > random(20)) and 0x2109 come first. 
 Outside codes 0x25, 0x2a..0x32, 0x60 and 0x61: by random(9) it comments 0x20df (and 0x20e0 by random(3); types 3 to 6 mark +0x16 and 0x20d9 by random(7)), passes the punishment's weight to the side's players (0x716450: the player himself, those on the pitch (p + 1) / 2, those off it p / 6 + 0.83) and 0x716e10 (1 on a sending-off); a sending-off removes the player (0x6cda20). 
 At the end, for each marked side and outside matches with a human manager who does not delegate: with +0x9049 the staff change the goalkeeper (0x6e1090 with 1), otherwise rebuild the team (0x6e1aa0), give the armband to the best-rated player (0x6e1a40/0x897760), zero +0xf59e/+0xf5a2 and recompose (0x6ce110); it stores the minute and recomputes strength and marking. 
 Ends with +0x1a3 = 0 and +0x8eb4 = 2.

The challenger won the ball on the shot (part of 0x702050, from 0x702f35 to 0x70353b): commentary, control or ball deflection, and the shooter's delay (+0x2b) and gains. \n The commentary (in his own area, 1 in 2, the foul one and 0x20e8/0x20ea/0x20eb; otherwise by incident, with the save 0x70d430 on incident 1); he controls it (0x6f0630, 0x70a890 with rating − shot − 200), the ball deflects below the incident's threshold (0x6cd770) or he aims for the side of the pitch; then the gains and the +0x2b of the player who shot.

`0x6b7f20` (ret 0x10, match_eng.cpp, 6 KB): prepares match `jogo` in the engine; returns 0 if the match had already ended. 
 It zeroes the state, the weather (+0x4756: 0x923010, 0x923970, 0x923630 in the original routine), the kits (0x6d47e0), the referee (0x6e9470) and the pitch conditions (0x85cba0, +0x91d2), both squads (0x6db500, with the error box below 11), the commentator (given or new, 0x6d5bf0), the strength of the sides and the marking. 
 The pre-match event list (0x68d020) receives the players unhappy with their contract (0x13), another club's interest (0x1e), form (5, 4) and contract expiry (6). 
 Without `rapida`, it draws who kicks off (+0x8eb6/+0x8eae) and set piece 8. Returns 0 if the match had already ended (+0x8eba).

`0x6cfe10` (ret 0x14, match_eng.cpp, ~2.6 KB) with the calls that change the game injected (0x62ed70 current injury, which first updates it; 0x6d0980 applies the injury): a tackle between `a` and `b` (incidents `tipo_a`/`tipo_b`) may injure either. 
 Each has a chance (random(random(102)), above 50 redone by random(random(76)) in 2/3) and a risk of 4 (6 if already injured, with the type's severity 0x62ec00 and the chance doubled in 24/25), adjusted by stamina (10000 / max(1000, +0x4d/2 + 5000)), by the player sheet (+0x2d, always `a`'s deciding the branch) and by the injury grade (0x62ece0). 
 `a` without stamina (< 4000) is injured on the spot (−1). With `direto`, only `a` is at risk: random(50000) below 10 × risk injures by severity, or by random(11). 
 Otherwise each one is at risk: whoever has the ball adds risk from the other's incident (the other's +0xd9 × table factor), incident 5 divides by +0x79; an injured player picks the type by severity (with the other player, 1..=9; without, 1..=5) or at random, and incident 5 has its own types (6, 9, 10).

`0x6bd930` (match_eng.cpp, `CM3_MATCH_ENGINE::period_completed`) with the calls that change the game injected (commentary 0x6d6f70, standings 0x6be120, summary 0x6ce460): closes the current period when the clock passes it (half time, full time, extra time, penalties); returns the next state. 
 It closes the period of +0x8ed4 when the clock (+0x8ed0) passes its end plus stoppage time (+0x8eb7). With +0x8eb2 = 5, nothing. Period 0 or 1: returns 4. 
 0x1ef (1st half): writes the half-time score to the match (+0x4792: +0x45/+0x46), comments 0x20f1, recovers stamina and moves to the 2nd half (returns 1). 
 0x3de (2nd half): writes the score (+0x43/+0x44); by the match rule (+0x38: 2 second leg, 4, 0x4000; 1 and 0x20 decide by penalties 4 or 1 at +0x8eb3) and the aggregate (+0x4b, +0x4c), it ends (4, with the standings commented, stamina ceiling and summary) or goes to extra time (comments 0x20f2, returns 2). 
 0x483 (extra time, 1st half): with +0x1a8 it ends; otherwise comments 0x20f3 and moves to the 2nd (3). 0x528: writes +0x47/+0x48 and ends, with penalties when the aggregate after extra time is level. 
 Unknown period: logs the error (0x944c9f) and returns 0, as when the clock has not passed.

`0x6ceb90` (match_eng.cpp): chooses the side's taker for set piece `tipo` (1..=8; 3 corner, 5 penalty, 6/7 free kick) as the highest-scoring of the 20 players in the block (the first tie stays). 
 Excluded: position < 0, or marked in `excluidos` (type 5). Position > 10 or no person (+0x6d): position becomes −1. The guarded goalkeeper (0xf59e/0xf5a2) does not take 1, 2, 3, 8, nor 6/7 far from the opposing area. 
 Scores: 1 and 2: attribute (0xdd, 0xe9) − 2 × distance to the ball; 3 (corner): the taker designated in the tactic (0x897990 on 0xde1d08; 10000/9000, with a random draw on the opposite side) or 0x89 − 0xad/2, × 0.75 (1.25 if negative) with mark 0x40 of the table; 4: 100 with table = 1; 5 (penalty): the human manager's list (10000 − order, 0x601070) or 0xc9 by age, random draw of the person's +0x5a and +0xb; 6/7 (free kick): near the goal, the designated taker or the person's set-piece ability (+0x29) and 0x109; far away, 0xa1 − distances; 8: 100 − distance. 
 Returns the match player; with nobody: 0 with `excluidos` (penalty shoot-out list), otherwise a fatal error.

`0x6e1aa0` (match_man.cpp) with the calls that change the game injected (0x6e0230 judges the line-up, 0x6e2000 picks the team, 0x6d6f70 commentary): the staff (`c`: +0x12 engine, +0x23 first of the 20 players, +0x2b tactic, +0x2f club) rebuild the team (formation check, selection, new positions and ratings for each player). \n With exactly 11 on the pitch and the line-up rejected (0x6e0230 with 0x8c1, 2) it comments 0x2007. \n Then it gathers the outfield players on the pitch (except table 1): position +0x19, tables 0x717410/0x717450, marks (0x5b5270) and byte (0x5b57c0) of the position and the player sheet +0x69; picks the team (0x6e2000 with 0x8800, or 0x408800 with a human manager to be consulted: 0x600a50, the staff's +0x19, the club's +0xcf, 0x5fd210, 0x5fea50 with 3) and gives each selected player sheet the position of the place it won, recomputing its performance (0x6eecb0).

The observer bonus (flag 0x1000): the knowledge `conhece` (+0x22 for the youngsters, +0x14, +0x0e, +0x1a, +0x1f, +0x13), the player's liking for the club and for `quem`, and the attributes of each position band. \n `craque_meia` also turns on the star players' bonus in band 0x20 (only in 0x6e6340).

The foul by `j` (type `t` from 0x6cfca0, incident `codigo`) punished by the referee (0x6cfd10) on the shot (0x6f6c00), identical to the stretch in 0x6f5c30; returns whether it was a penalty. \n 0x6f5c30 keeps its own inline copy: calling this function from there changes the career on 2002-01-12 without changing the logic (see PENDENCIAS). \n It does: 0x1fe8, card, set piece 7, penalty (5, −500 at +0x35 and, by random(the player sheet's +0x5a), an adjustment of +0x17 and the performance 0x6eecb0) or free kick (6), sending-off, taker (0x6ceb90) and the commentaries 0x21df to 0x21e2, and outside the special incidents 0x20df/0x20e0/0x20d9, the team's wear (0x6bb8d0) and fatigue.

`0x70c040` (ret 4, match_pl.cpp) with the calls that change things outside the engine injected (0x6d6f70 commentary, 0x6cd770 set piece, 0x716e10 and 0x6f0630; and those of the foul 0x6bac40): the outcome of player `p`'s shot with strength `f` (0 counts as 1). \n The quality (random(1000) − random(2000)) × (+0x8eaa + 1) / f against the goalkeeper's defence (0x6ce110, 0x700420, with rebound and coming out) gives the type: 1 on target, 2..11 wide (only the score 0x6ce310), 12/13 wide with a commented goal kick (0x1fca/0x1fcb, set piece 2). \n On target, the shot's share of the sum with the defence: above 71 it is a goal (penalty shoot-out 0x6bba50, golden goal 0x6d4250, the goalkeeper concedes; commentaries by score and time, 0x6bb950 on the side; the score +0xf5bd of the other side, the crowd commentaries), above 61 a save for a corner, above 51 a save that goes over the line (+0x8ea8, set piece 3 and 0x1f75), otherwise a save (0x6f0630); on saves, the goalkeeper's highlight (0x717470) chooses the commentary.

`0x70a910` (ret 4, match_pl.cpp) with the calls that change things outside the engine injected (as in 0x70c040): player `p`'s shot on goal with strength `f` (0 counts as 1), against the other side's goalkeeper (0x6ce110, 0x700420), with shot stats, goal counters, hat-trick and career marks. 
 Same type as in 0x70c040; outside the penalty shoot-out it counts the shot (+0xa) and the shot on target (+0xb); wide, it comments 0x1fc6..0x1fcb by type (8..13) and, with 12/13, the goal kick (0x211c). 
 Goal: +0xc, performance +0x89 and the five goal counts (+0x3d..+0x45, words); the score commentaries, the hat-trick (0x2011/0x1fd5) and the career marks (0x200a..0x2012 and the highlight 0x21b6, with the count as the last argument); the side's score +0xf5bd. 
 Saves as in 0x70c040 (0x211c instead of 0x211b).
Units of the dribbling tape: the copy of 0x68d0d0 goes to the list on the stack (a different address in the Rust copy: it writes without the `this`) and 0x702050 (the shot) is a unit.

`0x6f5810` (ret 4, match_pl.cpp): recovers the match player's stamina (+0x4d) or, with `teto`, sets its ceiling (+0x51), without random draws. 
 Without player data (+0x6d) nothing changes. The factor is 1, or 1.4 − 0.0004 × injury (0x62c3d0) above 1000. 
 Without `teto`: on the pitch (0x6c38c0 = 1) it adds 10 × (the player sheet's natural fitness +0x34 + 15) × factor; otherwise, off the bench (+0x19 >= 0), it adds 12 × fitness + 325 (with +0x1f = −1) or the same 10 × (fitness + 15); stamina stops at 10000. 
 With `teto`: +0x51 = stamina + (12 × fitness + 85) × factor, with the base multiplied by 5.56 × +0x20 − 255.76 when +0x20 (or +0x21 if the former is −1) is between 46 and 64; without both, on the bench the ceiling is the stamina. Out of play (+0x1c zero) and with a person, if the injury (0x62c590, up to 6500) exceeds the ceiling, the ceiling becomes 6500. 
 Finally the ceiling adds +0x59 and stops at 10000.
